patterns.label: Rhythm and Patterns
patterns.blurb: Work out the rule and carry the pattern on
patterns.intro: The pictures stand in a row by a rule, and they repeat. Work out the rule and say what should stand in place of the question mark!

shadows.label: Shadow Lotto
shadows.blurb: Find the shadow of each picture
shadows.intro: Every thing has a shadow — a black outline of the very same shape. Drag each picture onto its shadow!

mirror.label: The Mirror
mirror.blurb: Finish the other half — as in a mirror
mirror.intro: Only the left half of a picture is drawn here. The right half must be the same, only mirrored. Find it!

riddles.label: Logic Riddles
riddles.blurb: Little stories where you have to think, not count
riddles.intro: Listen to a short story and think. There is no need to count for long here — you have to work it out! If you need to, tap the speaker and I will read the riddle again.

patterns.1: Now the question mark stands in the middle of the row. Look at what repeats before it and after it.
patterns.2: The patterns are getting longer: now three different pictures repeat.
patterns.3: Careful: now pictures can stand in pairs — two of the same in a row.

shadows.1: Now the things on the board are of one kind — their shadows look more alike. Watch the little details!
shadows.2: Now the shadows come in pairs: two that look very alike, and two more that look very alike. Don’t mix them up!
shadows.3: The hardest part: all the shadows are almost the same, like those of a dog, a wolf and a fox. Look very carefully!

mirror.1: And now the halves of real pictures: a butterfly, a heart, a fir tree. Find the other half!
mirror.2: Now the halves look very much alike: they differ by one or two squares. Check each one!

riddles.1: Now we look for the rule: by what law do the numbers go? And we learn not to forget to count the one the story is about.
riddles.2: New riddles — about the days of the week, about cuts and pieces, and about what repeats in a circle.
riddles.3: Now the answer takes two steps: first find out one thing, and then the other.
riddles.4: The hardest of all: several clues at once. Cross out what cannot be — and the answer is left.

patterns.prompt: Which picture should stand in place of the question mark?
patterns.hint: Say the pictures out loud in order. A piece of {unit} pictures repeats here.

shadows.prompt: Find the shadow of each picture.
shadows.hint: Look closely at the outlines: ears, a tail, wheels. A shadow has the same shape as the picture.

mirror.prompt: This is the left half of a picture. Find the right one — just as in a mirror.
mirror.hint: Imagine a mirror in the middle. A square that stands next to the mirror on the left will stand next to it on the right too.
